images.alt: A Xerox 6085 Daybreak workstation with its keyboard, mouse and monitor on a desk
images.caption: The Xerox 6085 "Daybreak" — a full Star-derived desktop for about a third of the price of the 1981 original.

images.commonsFile: File:TSD Computer-, Schreib- und Bürotechnik Computer System Xerox 8010 - 6085 I.jpg
images.alt: A Xerox 8010/6085 computer system on display, showing the low flat case, keyboard and monitor together
images.caption: The low, flat 6085 case was built to fit under a desk, where its bulkier 1981 predecessor, the Xerox 8010 Star, would not.

images.commonsFile: File:TSD Computer -,Schreib und Bürotechnik Computer System Xerox 8010 - 6085 II.jpg
images.alt: A closer view of a Xerox 8010/6085 workstation's keyboard and monitor in a museum collection
images.caption: The Daybreak keyboard carried dedicated keys for the interface's verbs — NEXT, OPEN, PROPERTIES, MOVE, COPY — rather than menu shortcuts.

images.alt: A Xerox 8010/6085 workstation photographed in a technology museum, with monitor, keyboard and mouse
images.caption: By 1985 Xerox had renamed the Star environment ViewPoint and sold its applications as separately licensed options.

images.alt: A Xerox Daybreak-era workstation displayed among other historical computing equipment in a museum
images.caption: The 6085 shipped the same desktop vocabulary as the Star four years earlier — icons, windows, WYSIWYG editing — largely unmatched by contemporaries.
